title: Per-request routing and stream-aware load-shedding for multi-region hosted API
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Goal: implement a per-request, region-aware routing layer at the Edge Gateway that preserves stream/session continuity for long-lived connections while enabling safe active-active failover, circuit breaking, and prioritized load-shedding. This ticket defines design, trade-offs, and an incremental rollout plan to avoid cold-cache/mismatch failures for streaming clients and to meet revised SLOs for 99th percentile tail latency and availability across regions. Key constraints: short routing decision latency (<3ms added), minimal KV-cache invalidations on failover, graceful degradation of in-flight streams, and predictable unit cost impact.
acceptance_criteria: Per-request routing implemented with region-awareness and dynamic weight adjustment via Traffic Orchestration API
Active-active failover preserves streaming session continuity for >=95% of test flows in simulated region fault injections
Circuit breaker triggers at configured error-rate and latency thresholds and falls back to compatible model variants without user-facing 5xx for >=90% of degraded requests
Load-shedding policies apply per-customer and per-route priority, and shed non-essential traffic before essential chat/streaming workloads
End-to-end SLO dashboards show no regression in P50/P90 and <5% incremental cost at target traffic split for canary rollout
Runbook and automated rollback for regional failover testing completed and verified in staging
implementation_notes: Architecture: insert a routing proxy layer between edge ingress and gateway pool that queries a lightweight route-decider (local cache + periodic sync to control plane). Route-decider returns: region, pool-id, fallback policy, and stream-affinity token TTL

Session affinity: use per-connection affinity tokens stored in an encrypted cookie/header (short TTL) and replicated in KV cache keyed by connection-id. On region shift, proxy will attempt cross-region handoff when possible, otherwise initiate controlled buffered reconnect with preserved prompt prefix (KV cache snapshot).

Streaming preservation: for web-socket/http2 streams, implement pre-handoff drain window: stop accepting new tokens, signal upstream model to finish next logical chunk, then transfer last N tokens to fallback region. If transfer exceeds timeout, mark session degraded and apply UI-friendly event to client with reconnection hint.

Circuit breakers: hierarchical breakers (region level -> gateway pool -> model variant). Breaker state stored in control plane with TTL and local fast-path copy. Tripping rules: error-rate (>5% over 1m), sustained tail-latency (p99 > 2s for 30s), OOM or GPU-saturation signals. On trip, route to cheaper/quantized variant or queue short requests based on priority.

Load-shedding: implement priority buckets (essential chat streaming, interactive short-gen, background embeddings). Shedding strategy: reject/queue/redirect based on bucket with preemption; provide explainable 429 with retry-after for rejected flows. Keep metrics to measure false-positive shedding.

KV cache handling: to minimize invalidation, use multi-region cache replication with last-writer-wins metadata. On failover, prefer warm copies within allowed staleness window (configurable up to 5s).
Observability: add per-request trace tags for routing-decision, affinity-token, breaker-action, shed-reason and attach to existing Console dashboards and traces.

Trade-offs considered: synchronous cross-region handoff increases latency and complexity; chosen approach favors best-effort handoff + graceful reconnect to bound complexity. Kubernetes-proxy vs custom proxy: chosen custom lightweight proxy for deterministic latency and easier control-plane hooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Simulation (staging): run traffic replay and fault-injection to validate handoff and breaker behavior against synthetic streams
Phase 1 - Canary (0.5% traffic): enable per-request routing for non-streaming short-gen routes and monitor SLOs for 24h
Phase 2 - Streaming canary (1% traffic): enable stream-affinity tokens and handoff for low-concurrency test tenants
Phase 3 - Regional failover drills (5% traffic): run scheduled simulated region outage and measure continuity metrics
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp (5%->50%->100% over 2 weeks): enable full policy including shedding and hierarchical circuit breakers with ops on-call monitoring

Rollback criteria: any sustained P99 latency regression >25% over baseline for 30m, increase in user-visible 5xx >0.5% absolute, or shedding rate causing >1% drop in successful essential-stream sessions
testing_plan: Unit tests for route-decider logic and affinity token lifecycle
Integration tests: proxy <-> gateway pool transitions using local control-plane mocks
Fault injection: drop region, simulate GPU OOM, induce p99 latency spikes, and validate fallback correctness
Chaos tests: randomized network partitions to measure KV-cache staleness effects
Canary validation harness: synthetic streaming clients that validate message order and prefix preservation after handoff
observability_requirements: New metrics: routing_decision_latency_ms, handoff_success_rate, affinity_token_miss_rate, breaker_trips_per_min, shed_rate_by_priority
Tracing: add routing.* and breaker.* spans with correlation_id and model_variant tags
Dashboard: per-region failover dashboard with SLO gating and real-time counts for shed/rejected/redirected requests
Alerts: PagerDuty for handoff_success_rate <95% for 10m, breaker_trips spike >3x baseline, shed_rate for essential bucket >0.5%
